<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8dfd1265f006ea0a6f727fa966e980ede57b4214`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8dfd1265f006ea0a6f727fa966e980ede57b4214` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9241b0a5f06ea0e80e85255206b05e676d999db6` — the merge of head `d92ef224efbadb063823a0210fc52ae5574f1886` into base `8dfd1265f006ea0a6f727fa966e980ede57b4214`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9241b0a5f06ea0e80e85255206b05e676d999db6 && git checkout 9241b0a5f06ea0e80e85255206b05e676d999db6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8dfd1265f006ea0a6f727fa966e980ede57b4214 d92ef224efbadb063823a0210fc52ae5574f1886 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8dfd1265f006ea0a6f727fa966e980ede57b4214 && git merge --no-ff d92ef224efbadb063823a0210fc52ae5574f1886

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8dfd1265f006ea0a6f727fa966e980ede57b4214
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8dfd1265f006ea0a6f727fa966e980ede57b4214` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Seat ACCEPT · epic PM `session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3` (`os-steve`) · 2026-10-22T19:49Z. PR #25272 at `d92ef224efbadb063823a0210fc52ae5574f1886` (#25206; claim 6345859138; measurement 6346714622, recommendation A). **ACCEPT.**

## Seat check

- **Shape:** 5 files, +356 / −4, all in `packages/cli` plus one changeset. `check-governed-merges --pr 25272`: not governed, so this is an ordinary queue landing.
- **Review tier:** no contract face is touched. The PR declares `Clause-②: no`, changes no published schema, touches no governed path, and declares no narrowing. So the review is CI plus this seat read, and no second agent.
- **What it does** (ADR-0131 D10, the ceremony's fate 3; #24343 A3):
  - Under a wall only, the ceremony gives an organization-less `sys_user_permission_set` self-registration grant the organization of its user's sole membership, meaning the case where every stamped `sys_member` row of the user names one organization.
  - It reports, and neither guesses nor deletes: a user in several organizations, a user in none, and a key the grant's unique index would refuse. That last check covers both an existing row and a second NULL row in the same pass.
  - `single` is unchanged: the Default Organization takes the grant.
- **Seat read of the code:**
  - `applySoleMembership` runs after the inventory anchors, only when `fate === 'attribution'` and the posture is not `single`.
  - The membership read takes stamped rows only (`organization_id IS NOT NULL`), chunked.
  - The collision check runs per key column against the table and the walk's own `taken` set.
  - The derived count is labelled `sole-membership` (from `user_id` to `sys_member`).
  - The inventory key `soleMembership` is platform-only; the spec supplement has none.
  - Noted, not blocking: a user's NULL-organization `sys_member` rows are ignored when the sole organization is judged. Such a row is itself reported and holds certification, so the operator meets it in the same plan.
  - The inventory change moves the inventory digest, so a plan file written before this release is refused at `--apply` and must be re-planned. That is the existing contract.
- **CI on the head:** the latest run of every check is success or skipped. That includes `Test Core`, `Check Changeset` and the labelled `18.x upgrade harness` lane.
- **R1–R4,** measured by the dev on this head:
  - R2 and R3: the harness passed 16/16, both fixture legs plus the fresh store.
  - R1: a production `os serve` under `single`, `isolated` and `group` answered health 200.
  - R4: a walled store with 4 legacy NULL grants went through the ceremony. 1 grant was attributed and 3 reported, and the boot guard refused the uncertified store. After the operator's hand fix, the ceremony completed and a walled `os serve` was ready, with sign-in 200.
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/cli` `patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Right: no authorable key moves.
- **Landing:** the seat flips the PR ready and enables auto-merge. `Fixes #25206` closes the card. #24343 then waits on #25207 alone.
